summary: Unbalanced GPU utilization during cross-tenant burst causes elevated p95 and request timeouts in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 08:40 UTC SageDocs observed a sudden rise in p95 latency and intermittent 504/502 timeouts for inference requests served from their dedicated GPU reservation in us-west-2. Impact: Customer-facing inference calls periodically fail or exceed the 3s p95 target, causing feature degradation in their document summarization flow. Environment: Dedicated reservation ID dr-0456 (us-west-2), provisioned 4x A100-40GB. Traffic profile: mixed short-chat and long-seq summarization jobs with burst at customer-defined schedule windows.
impact: ~12% of SageDocs' requests during burst window returned 5xx or timed out; sustained p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.8s for 30-90 minute periods. Business impact: upstream job batchers report retry storms; customer reports visible UX errors affecting paid users.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route synthetic mixed-length traffic (30% long-seq >1024 tokens, 70% short <128 tokens) at 1.8x baseline QPS into the dedicated reservation during a 10-minute ramp. 2) Observe per-pod GPU util and queue lengths. 3) Confirm that requests targeting the same GPU slice see increased tail latency while other slices remain underutilized.
logs_and_metrics:
- Pod metrics (2026-03-13T08:42 - 09:55 UTC): gpu_util between affected pods hits 98-100% while sibling pods at 35-60%.
- Scheduler queue depth spikes: microbatch queue length 4x baseline.
- Autoscaler events: no scale-up events recorded during initial 20m of burst; cooldowns prevented additional nodes.
- Relevant traces: trace IDs /traces/0a1b2c3d shows wait times in queue layer before entering runtime.
- Monitoring alerts: node-gpu-thermal-warning (cleared), but no kernel OOMs recorded.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:05 UTC - Support (Aisha): Informed customer we are investigating; asked for recent request logs and exact time windows.
2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - SRE (Marcus): Initial hypothesis: autoscaler mis-sizing + imbalanced pod placement causing GPU hot spots. Kicking off allocation review.
2026-03-13 09:30 UTC - Customer (SageDocs - Elena): Peak started at 08:36 UTC; we pushed a campaign causing higher proportion of long sequences. Asking for ETA on mitigation.
2026-03-13 10:01 UTC - Eng (Marcus): Manual rebalancing attempted (evict & reschedule low-priority pods) to spread load; observed immediate p95 improvement in two intervals.
2026-03-14 07:20 UTC - Eng (Marcus): Working on autoscaler config patch and placement policy change; created PR to avoid colocating large-seq heavy pods on same node.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Noisy neighbor - one tenant's long-seq batch jobs saturated a subset of GPU slices and prevented fair scheduling of short requests.
Evidence: skewed gpu_util per-pod, queueing before runtime.
Status: supported by metrics.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler cooling/caps prevented required scale-up during ramp.
Evidence: no scale events despite rising queue depth; autoscaler logs show cooldowns and a max-allowed increase cap tied to reservation plan.
Status: supported; policy limits observed.

Hypothesis 3: Inefficient batch packing for mixed sequence-length traffic increased microbatch durations, raising head-of-line blocking.
Evidence: increased microbatch latencies in traces, higher KV cache churn on affected GPUs.
Status: partial.
Temporary mitigation tested: manual pod reschedule + reduced long-seq QPS (customer side) resulted in p95 improvement from ~1.8s -> ~420ms within 8 minutes.
Affected component owners: serving-runtime (ops), autoscaler (infra), scheduler (placement).
resolution: Mitigation applied (workaround): 1) Manual rebalancing performed to spread heavy long-seq jobs across nodes. 2) Temporary split routing rule created for SageDocs to route long-seq traffic to a dedicated subset of nodes to avoid cross-tenant interference. 3) Customer agreed to throttle campaign by 30% during the next 48h window. Long-term fix: autoscaler config PR #1987 to relax cooldown for dedicated reservations and a placement policy change to bin-pack long-seq into dedicated slices. Follow-ups: validate patch in staging and schedule a maintenance window to roll out placement change.
resolution_notes:
- PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1987 (autoscaler/cooldown changes).
- Follow-up runbook update: 'Dedicated-pool noisy neighbor' to include cross-tenant split-routing guidance.
- Customer follow-up: monitoring dashboard shared; support to confirm post-rollout latency trends for 72 hours.
next_steps: Merge and deploy autoscaler cooldown/limit change after performance validation in staging (owner: infra)
Implement placement policy to avoid co-locating long-seq heavy pods with latency-critical tenants (owner: scheduler)
Coordinate with SageDocs to enable long-seq dedicated routing permanently if traffic mix persists
Add automated alert rule for skewed per-pod GPU util >80% while cluster-level avg <60%
